articles.headline: The oldest grudge in football
articles.description: When Texas Tech and its brash benefactor bought their way into the college football big time, they were settling an old West Texas score.

images.name: Texas Tech [1296x729]
images.caption: Behind the vision and backing of billionaire donor Cody Campbell, coach Joey McGuire and the Red Raiders have embraced a role of disruptors as college football's villians and are trying to become a new power.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 1 [946x947]
images.caption: The Santa Rita No. 1 ushered in a new era of oil exploration in the Permian Basin.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 2 [2929x2000]
images.alt: The oil that won World War II.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 3 [2693x1616]
images.caption: Preston Smith (right) was the first Texas governor from West Texas. He was a student at Texas Technological College.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 4 [2933x1339]
images.caption: The original Four Sixes barn from 1908 is now on the Texas Tech campus at the National Ranching Heritage Center.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 5 [2000x3000]
images.caption: Four relief carvings on the facade of a building at Texas Tech.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 6 [1987x1365]
images.caption: Cody Campbell, a fourth-generation Red Raider, and his son, Carson, a 2029 recruit, talking to Pat McAfee on the "College GameDay" set.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 7 [2999x1940]
images.caption: Vintage oil and gas signs at Cooks Garage in Lubbock.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 8 [2999x1999]
images.caption: Lugene Pickering, the 1975 Texas Tech homecoming queen, has been a devoted Red Raiders fan since birth and makes a homemade cobbler for coach Joey McGuire and takes it to his house to show her appreciation after each Tech win.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 11 [2836x1860]
images.caption: Texas Tech's Masked Rider, Sofie Jones, leads the charge onto the field before every Red Raiders game, a proud tradition. Left, trophies commemorate Texas Tech players who have won Super Bowls.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 12 [2625x1333]
images.caption: There isn't much cover from the wide-open skies in West Texas, but red-and-black-clad fans are accustomed to handling an unpredictable environment.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 13 [1601x1020]
images.caption: Taylor Sheridan, part of a group that owns the legendary Four Sixes Ranch, has long admired Texas Tech football. Right, Eclipse Windmills were used across the West Texas to drill for water on ranches and hauled onto job sites like building railroads.

images.name: Texas Tech - 36x [1785x1494]
images.caption: Texas Tech owes a lot, past and present, to the oilfield, and proudly displays its pride, including T-shirts that say "Thank you for filling up your gas tank" with the Red Raiders' Double-T logo on them.
images.alt: An old oil rig painted in Texas Tech colors.

images.name: Texas Tech - 35x [2999x2000]
images.caption: Former Texas coach Mack Brown said coaching against Texas Tech in Lubbock was a challenge: "They do have an edge. They love their land, they love their town. Anybody who says anything bad about any of it is not going to be taken well."

article.headline: Smith runs for 121 yards and 2 TDs, No. 14 Oregon routs Michigan St 45-7 holding onto playoff hopes

article.linkText: Smith runs for 121 yards and 2 TDs, No. 14 Oregon routs Michigan St 45-7 holding onto playoff hopes
article.story: EAST LANSING, Mich. -- — No. 14 Oregon routed Michigan State 45-7 on Friday night, trying to show that they deserve a spot in the College Football Playoff. “We’re certainly an exciting team to watch,” Ducks coach Dan Lanning said. Oregon (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten) has won four straight games, climbing to No. 13 in the CFP rankings with time running out to play its way into the 12-team playoff, heading into the final regular season game against rival Washington. “No love lost,” Lanning said. Brandon Smith set career highs with 121 yards and two touchdowns — filling in for Dierre Hill — and kicker Gage Hurych ran for a 15-yard score on a fake field goal for the Ducks. The Spartans (3-8, 1-7) made costly mistakes in the second quarter, hurting their chances to stay competitive before getting outscored 28-7 in the second half. “We didn't give ourselves a chance to win in those two quarters,” coach Pat Fitzgerald said. While Oregon did win the game, it lost another player in the backfield due to injury. Smith limped off the field in the first quarter after getting tackled and was on crutches in the second half with a boot on his left leg. “I don’t anticipate this being a long-term injury,” Lanning said. Oregon running back Jordon Davison missed his third straight game with a leg injury and quarterback Dante Moore has not played since getting concussed in the fourth game of the season. Smith, who was the team's third-string running back, broke a scoreless tie with a 5-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter and the freshman also ran for a 1-yard touchdown in the third. “Brandon has been getting more and more reps that allowed him to perform,” Lanning said. Lanning pulled off another trick play in the final seconds of the first half to put his team ahead 17-0. Bailey Ettridge took the snap, put the ball on the grass and pitched it to Hurych, who sprinted to the left and broke a tackle on a touchdown run that showed some of the athleticism that helped him have five offers to play Division I lacrosse. “The guy can dunk it,” Lanning said. “He’s an athlete.” Michigan State scored on Jaziun Patterson's 1-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter. The Spartans were in Oregon territory twice in the second quarter, but Liam Boyd missed a 47-yard kick and freshman quarterback Kayd Coffman stumbled to the ground without getting touched on a fourth-down run. Michigan State punt returner Chrishon McCray lost a fumble on a punt return, setting up Hurych's 40-yard field goal in the pivotal quarter. Coffman, starting for a second time for the injured Alessio Milivojevic, was 10 of 19 for 106 yards with an interception. Oregon's Dylan Raiola completed 21 of 34 passes for 234 yards with a 31-yard touchdown pass to Dakorien Moore, who made a one-handed catch in the end zone. The takeaway Oregon: Trying to climb in the CFP rankings with a large margin of victory, Raiola was throwing passes late in the fourth quarter to set up another touchdown to take a 38-point lead. “I thought it was important to continue to operate,” Lanning said. Earlier in the week, Fitzgerald said the Ducks were more talented than the Notre Dame and the UCLA team he faced this season. “I was right," Fitzgerald said. “Wasn't I?” Michigan State: Fitzgerald is about a week away from turning his focus to next year after a disappointing debut season as the latest coach tasked with turning around a program that has had five straight seasons with losing records. Fitzgerald, though, has been pleased with his team's effort. “I’m really proud of these guys,” he said. Lanning said he respects Fitzgerald, who he believes will turn the Spartans into a winner. “He’s building something here,” Lanning said. Up next Oregon host Washington on Nov. 28. Michigan State ends the season at Rutgers on Nov. 28. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here. Visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college football coverage here.
